topicTitle: Latent Heat and the Clausius-Clapeyron Equation

questions.prompt: Using the model for Latent Heat and the Clausius-Clapeyron Equation, set up the governing equation, inequality, derivative, probability, or phase-rule count and solve the following problem: At \(300\,\mathrm K\), a transition has \(L_m=6.0\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}\) and \(\Delta V_m=2.0\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}\). Calculate \(dp/dT\).
questions.answer:
Model:
Apply the model for Latent Heat and the Clausius-Clapeyron Equation under every condition stated in the question; use SI units unless another unit is explicitly supplied.

Working:
Use equation \([3]\) because both quantities are molar: \[\frac{dp}{dT}=\frac{6.0\times10^3\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}}{(300\,\mathrm K)(2.0\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}})}=1.0\times10^6\,\mathrm{Pa\,K^{-1}}.\] The units reduce because \(\mathrm J=\mathrm{Pa\,m^3}\). Final result: \(dp/dT=1.0\times10^6\,\mathrm{Pa\,K^{-1}}\).

Final answer:
\(dp/dT=1.0\times10^6\,\mathrm{Pa\,K^{-1}}\).

Check:
Substituting the result back into the defining relation reproduces the stated data to the quoted precision. The final unit follows from the equation, and the qualitative trend agrees with the model.

questions.answer:
Model:
Apply the model for Latent Heat and the Clausius-Clapeyron Equation under every condition stated in the question; use SI units unless another unit is explicitly supplied.

Working:
Melting absorbs heat, so \(L_m\gt 0\). Liquid water near the ordinary melting point has a smaller molar volume than ice, so \(\Delta V_m=V_{m,\mathrm l}-V_{m,\mathrm s}\lt 0\). Equality of molar chemical potentials along the boundary links this molar latent heat and the molar volume change to the boundary slope through the Clapeyron equation. \qquad
